children: Indrocorp Technologies Inc., doing business as Indrotek, filed a Form F-1 to register its initial U.S. public offering of common shares. The company has not disclosed the number of shares, price range, or expected offering proceeds in this preliminary filing. It has applied to list its shares on an unnamed U.S. national securities exchange under a ticker that has not yet been disclosed.

Indrotek is a Canadian technology company with three operating divisions. InDro Robotics designs, assembles and integrates drones, ground robots and other robotic systems, and provides engineering, software, testing and operational services. Bravo Zulu sells counter-drone detection and mitigation equipment, including jamming and radar-based systems, and is developing related software capabilities. Stratocom provides aerial utility-meter reading and other data-collection services using aircraft equipped with specialized equipment.

The company earns revenue from UAV and multi-domain robotics products and services, aerial data collection, and related engineering work. Its stated strengths include experience with specialized Canadian flight permissions, systems integration across different robotic platforms, and relationships with government, industry and research partners. The filing also describes the company as reliant on financing, with a history of losses and substantial debt.

: The filing cites third-party estimates valuing the global utility-drone market at approximately US$591.57 million in 2025 and the global anti-drone market at approximately US$3.07 billion in 2025; the global artificial-intelligence-robot market is projected at US$6.11 billion in 2025.

: Cited forecasts project the utility-drone market to reach US$4.58 billion by 2032, the anti-drone market to reach US$19.69 billion by 2033, and the AI-robot market to reach US$33.39 billion by 2030.

: Indrotek describes itself as an early Canadian BVLOS drone operator and says its InDro Robotics subsidiary has qualified under all five streams of Canada’s Defence Drone Initiative Marketplace; qualification does not guarantee contracts or revenue.

: The filing identifies Blighter Surveillance Systems, ClearGrid, Dedrone, D-Fend Solutions, Draganfly, Drone Delivery Canada, Plymouth Rock Technology and Skylock Industries across relevant product and service categories.

: The filing points to growing use of drones and robots for infrastructure inspection, industrial monitoring and defense, alongside advances in autonomy, AI-enabled analytics, sensors and counter-drone detection and mitigation.
: Stratocom collects data for approximately 113,000 utility meters per month in Alberta.
: The filing reports 25 full-time employees and 14 full-time consultants; it separately describes an InDro Robotics engineering team of more than 30 personnel.
: InDro Robotics describes a roughly 5,000-square-foot prototyping and assembly facility near Ottawa and uses testing facilities in Ottawa and at the Killaloe aerodrome in Ontario.

: The company is headquartered in Vancouver, with operations and facilities in Ontario and aerial data-collection activity in Alberta; it reports revenue from Canada, the United States and other markets.
: The filing describes work or collaborations involving Google, Microsoft, NASA, Nokia, Rogers, Transport Canada, Ericsson, Honeywell, the University of British Columbia, LFL Group and Lemay.ai.

: InDro Robotics qualified under all five streams of Canada’s Defence Drone Initiative Marketplace and received a supply arrangement for Stream 1; this qualification is not a specific purchase order or revenue commitment.
: One Canadian robotics-company customer accounted for C$618,568, or 16% of consolidated revenue, in the six months ended March 31, 2026.
: C$3,779,960 for the six months ended March 31, 2026.
: 43% year over year compared with the six months ended March 31, 2025.
: Net loss of C$2,953,094 for the six months ended March 31, 2026.
, President, Chief Executive Officer and Director - Company co-founder with experience in oilfield operations, pipeline construction, business development and utility data collection.

, Chief Financial Officer - Finance and robotics executive who previously served as president of Richtech Robotics and has experience with public-company operations, capital markets and technology commercialization.
, Director and founder of InDro Robotics - Technology and commercial-aviation entrepreneur with experience in UAV development, BVLOS operations and robotics engineering.
: Manufacturing expansion, equipment purchases, research and development, debt settlements, working capital and general corporate purposes.
